title: Home inspector radon testing in home sales practice questions
description: Practice questions on EPA radon testing guidance for home sales: who should test, test types, placement, test conditions and results.

questions.question: A buyer says nobody in the seller's family has had health problems and the house "seems fine," so a radon test looks unnecessary. What does the Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide say?

options.A: A home inspector's visual inspection can show whether radon is a problem
options.B: Testing is needed only where neighbors found high levels
options.C: Testing is the only way to know if you and your family are at risk from radon
options.D: Testing is needed only if someone in the home has symptoms

questions.explanation: The guide says: "Testing is the only way to know if you and your family are at risk from radon." It adds that "EPA and the Surgeon General recommend testing all homes below the third floor for radon."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: Testing is the only way to know if you and your family are at risk from radon.

questions.question: A buyer learns that the house next door tested low for radon. What does EPA's Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide say about using that result?

options.A: Do not rely on it to estimate the radon level in the home being bought
options.B: It may replace a test if it is less than two years old
options.C: It is reliable because homes next to each other have the same radon level
options.D: It may be used if the state radon office approves it

questions.explanation: The guide says "Do not rely on radon test results taken in other homes in the neighborhood to estimate the radon level in your home" and that "Homes which are next to each other can have different indoor radon levels."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: Do not rely on radon test results taken in other homes in the neighborhood to estimate the radon level in your home. Homes which are next to each other can have different indoor radon levels.

questions.question: A buyer who smokes asks whether radon matters for him, since he "already has a risk." What does EPA's Health Risk of Radon page say?

options.A: Radon causes lung cancer only in people who have never smoked
options.B: A smoker who is also exposed to radon has a much higher risk of lung cancer
options.C: Smoking cancels out the effect of radon exposure
options.D: Radon matters only for children under 6

questions.explanation: The page says: "A smoker who is also exposed to radon has a much higher risk of lung cancer." Its heading says "Exposure to radon causes lung cancer in non-smokers and smokers alike".

source.title: EPA: Health Risk of Radon (retrieved Nov 15, 2026)

questions.evidence: A smoker who is also exposed to radon has a much higher risk of lung cancer.

questions.topic: Selling a home: what EPA recommends
questions.question: When does EPA recommend that a seller test the home for radon?

options.A: Only after a buyer asks for a test
options.B: Only if the state requires radon disclosure
options.C: After the sale closes
options.D: Before putting the home on the market

questions.explanation: "EPA recommends that you test your home before putting it on the market and, if necessary, lower your radon levels."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: EPA recommends that you test your home before putting it on the market and, if necessary, lower your radon levels.

questions.topic: Selling a home: what EPA recommends
questions.question: A seller already tested the home for radon. What does the guide tell the seller to do with that test?

options.A: Send the results to EPA for approval
options.B: Review the Radon Testing Checklist to make sure the test was done correctly and, if so, provide the results to the buyer
options.C: Keep the results private unless the buyer files a complaint
options.D: Replace it with a long-term test before listing

questions.explanation: The seller should "review the Radon Testing Checklist to make sure that the test was done correctly. If so, provide your test results to the buyer."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: review the Radon Testing Checklist to make sure that the test was done correctly. If so, provide your test results to the buyer.

questions.topic: Selling a home: what EPA recommends
questions.question: The seller's radon test was taken on the first floor. The buyer plans to use the basement regularly. What does the guide say the buyer may do?

options.A: Ask for a new test
options.B: Nothing, because a first-floor result covers the whole house
options.C: Use the seller's result only if it is under 2 pCi/L
options.D: Require EPA to inspect the basement

questions.explanation: A potential buyer may ask for a new test, especially if "The buyer plans to use a lower level of the house than was tested, such as a basement that could be used regularly by the buyer."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: The buyer plans to use a lower level of the house than was tested, such as a basement that could be used regularly by the buyer.

questions.topic: Buying a home: what EPA recommends
questions.question: Before accepting the seller's radon test, which of these does the guide say the buyer should determine?

options.A: The brand of the seller's heating system
options.B: How much the seller paid for the test
options.C: Who conducted the previous test: the homeowner, a radon professional, or some other person
options.D: Whether the seller has ever smoked

questions.explanation: The buyer should determine "Who conducted the previous test: the homeowner, a radon professional, or some other person."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: Who conducted the previous test: the homeowner, a radon professional, or some other person;

questions.topic: Buying a home: what EPA recommends
questions.question: The home has not been tested. Which contract provision does the guide suggest the buyer consider?

options.A: A promise that the radon level is below 2 pCi/L
options.B: A waiver of any radon testing
options.C: A clause that EPA will conduct the test
options.D: How the seller and the buyer will share the test results and test costs (if necessary)

questions.explanation: The guide suggests "provisions in the contract specifying" items including "How the seller and the buyer will share the test results and test costs (if necessary)."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: How the seller and the buyer will share the test results and test costs (if necessary); and

questions.topic: Buying a home: what EPA recommends
questions.question: A buyer decides to use a qualified radon tester. Whom does the guide tell the buyer to contact for a copy of an approved list of radon testing companies?

options.A: The seller's real estate agent
options.B: The local building department
options.C: The EPA regional office
options.D: The state radon office

questions.explanation: "If you decide to use a qualified radon tester, contact your state radon office to obtain a copy of their approved list of radon testing companies."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: If you decide to use a qualified radon tester, contact your state radon office to obtain a copy of their approved list of radon testing companies.

questions.question: How does the guide describe the difference between passive and active radon testing devices?

options.A: Passive devices are used only for long-term tests; active devices only for short-term tests
options.B: Passive devices do not need power to function; active devices require power
options.C: Passive devices are read in the home; active devices are sent to a lab
options.D: Passive devices are for sellers; active devices are for buyers

questions.explanation: "Passive radon testing devices do not need power to function" while "Active radon testing devices require power to function."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: Passive radon testing devices do not need power to function.

questions.question: A seller's agent wants a radon result before an open house and suggests running a 24-hour test. What does the Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide say about test length?

options.A: All radon tests should be taken for a minimum of 48 hours, whether you test yourself or hire a qualified tester
options.B: A 24-hour test is acceptable when a qualified tester runs it
options.C: Any test length is acceptable as long as closed-house conditions are kept
options.D: The minimum length applies only to long-term tests

questions.explanation: The guide says: "Whether you test for radon yourself or hire a qualified tester, all radon tests should be taken for a minimum of 48 hours." Some devices require a longer minimum.

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: Whether you test for radon yourself or hire a qualified tester, all radon tests should be taken for a minimum of 48 hours.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the three short-term testing options the guide gives for real estate transactions?

options.A: One passive test in a crawl space for 24 hours
options.B: One test on each floor taken in different weeks
options.C: Test the home with a continuous monitor for at least 48 hours
options.D: A test kit left open in the kitchen for one day

questions.explanation: The active option is to "Test the home with a continuous monitor for at least 48 hours."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: Test the home with a continuous monitor for at least 48 hours.

questions.question: Which of these places does the guide name as a place not to test?

options.A: A hallway
options.B: A den
options.C: A family room
options.D: A workshop

questions.explanation: "Do not test in a closet, stairway, hallway, crawl space or in an enclosed area of high humidity or high air velocity."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: Do not test in a closet, stairway, hallway, crawl space or in an enclosed area of high humidity or high air velocity.

questions.question: In which level of the home does EPA recommend placing the radon test device(s)?

options.A: The top floor, where bedrooms usually are
options.B: Only a finished level
options.C: The level the seller uses most
options.D: The lowest level that could be used regularly, whether it is finished or unfinished

questions.explanation: "EPA recommends that the test device(s) be placed in the lowest level of the home that could be used regularly, whether it is finished or unfinished."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: EPA recommends that the test device(s) be placed in the lowest level of the home that could be used regularly, whether it is finished or unfinished.

questions.question: During a 3-day short-term radon test, the seller plans to open the windows on the second afternoon to air out the house. What does the Radon Testing Checklist say?

options.A: Windows may be opened once the first 24 hours of the test have passed
options.B: Maintain closed-house conditions for at least 12 hours before the beginning of the test and during the entire test period
options.C: Windows may be opened during the day if they are closed at night
options.D: Closed-house conditions matter only for tests longer than one week

questions.explanation: The checklist says: "When doing a short-term test ranging from 2-4 days, it is important to maintain closed-house conditions for at least 12 hours before the beginning of the test and during the entire test period."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: When doing a short-term test ranging from 2-4 days, it is important to maintain closed-house conditions for at least 12 hours before the beginning of the test and during the entire test period.

questions.question: Under closed-house conditions as the guide defines them, which of these may run during the test?

options.A: A window fan that brings in outside air
options.B: A whole-house fan that brings in air from outside
options.C: Small exhaust fans operating for only short periods of time
options.D: Any fan, as long as the windows stay closed

questions.explanation: Closed-house conditions include "not operating fans or other machines which bring in air from outside," but "Fans that are part of a radon-reduction system or small exhaust fans operating for only short periods of time may run during the test."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: Fans that are part of a radon-reduction system or small exhaust fans operating for only short periods of time may run during the test.

questions.question: The home has an active radon-reduction system, and its vent fan is not operating properly. What does the checklist say to do?

options.A: Switch the system off and test without it
options.B: Test first, then repair the fan if the result is high
options.C: Skip the test because the system is installed
options.D: Have it (or ask to have it) repaired and then test

questions.explanation: "If the fan is not operating properly, have it (or ask to have it) repaired and then test."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: If the fan is not operating properly, have it (or ask to have it) repaired and then test.

questions.topic: Testing yourself or hiring a qualified tester
questions.question: In states that don't regulate radon services, what does the guide suggest asking a contractor?

options.A: Whether they hold a professional proficiency or certification credential
options.B: Whether they will guarantee a result below 4 pCi/L
options.C: Whether they are related to the seller
options.D: Whether they hold a real estate license

questions.explanation: "In states that don't regulate radon services, ask the contractor if they hold a professional proficiency or certification credential."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: In states that don't regulate radon services, ask the contractor if they hold a professional proficiency or certification credential.

questions.question: A test shows a radon level between 2 and 4 pCi/L. What does the guide say?

options.A: No action is needed because levels below 4 pCi/L carry no risk
options.B: The result must be reported to EPA
options.C: Consider fixing when the radon level is between 2 and 4 pCi/L
options.D: Retest only after two years

questions.explanation: "A radon level below 4 pCi/L still poses a risk. Consider fixing when the radon level is between 2 and 4 pCi/L."

source.title: EPA: Home Buyer's and Seller's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-24/001, revised March 2024)

questions.evidence: A radon level below 4 pCi/L still poses a risk. Consider fixing when the radon level is between 2 and 4 pCi/L.

questions.question: In A Citizen's Guide to Radon, what should you do if your first short-term test result is more than twice EPA's 4 pCi/L action level?

options.A: Wait until the next season and test again
options.B: Take a second short-term test immediately
options.C: Move the test kit to an upper floor
options.D: Accept the result without a follow-up test

questions.explanation: "If your first short-term test result is more than twice EPA's 4 pCi/L action level, you should take a second short-term test immediately."

source.title: EPA: A Citizen's Guide to Radon (EPA 402/K-12/002, 2025 edition)

questions.evidence: If your first short-term test result is more than twice EPA's 4 pCi/L action level, you should take a second short-term test immediately.
